Since \(B\) is the midpoint of \(QR\), we have \(QB=12/2=6\). In \(\triangle PBQ\), the angle between \(PB\) and \(PQ\) is \(\alpha=60^\circ\). By the sine rule,

\[
\frac{\sin \angle PBQ}{PQ}=\frac{\sin 60^\circ}{QB}
\]

so

\[
\sin \angle PBQ=\frac{8\sin 60^\circ}{6}
=\frac{8\cdot \frac{\sqrt3}{2}}{6}
=\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}>1,
\]

which is impossible. Therefore no such triangle \(PQR\) exists, so the least possible length of \(XZ\) is undefined.

\[
\boxed{\text{No such triangle exists}}
\]
